cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Make It Official
cards.instruction: Recruit someone by giving them a title, role, or ceremonial duty that makes participation feel binding.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. Would you be honorary patron of our roof appeal? You'd open it and thank the donors. Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can come, but I won't make a speech.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. Then accept the patron's ribbon and lead the applause. That can be your ceremonial duty.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I leave after the first donation?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The patron applauds every donor. We couldn't have the later ones thinking their money mattered less.

mechanism: A recruits a roof-appeal patron by replacing speech with applause and shortening the program while keeping the title responsible for every donor acknowledgment.
confusable: Unlike simply asking attendance, the ribbon and patron duty make continued participation binding.
comparison: Public donor applause differs from appointing a successor for a festival lantern.
seedUse: D175-b honorary patron, no speech and first donation; S02-b takes talking and promises brisk names.
